name: Khan Academy — Khanmigo
dinh_nghia: Khanmigo is Khan Academy's AI-powered tutoring and teaching assistant, launched March 2023, built on OpenAI's GPT-4. It is designed around a Socratic pedagogy: the AI guides students through reasoning by asking questions rather than providing direct answers. The key academic integrity design principle is that Khanmigo cannot be used as a cheating tool — it refuses to write essays, complete assignments, or produce work that students would submit as their own. This makes Khanmigo an example of 'integrity-by-design' AI in education.
phan_loai: Khanmigo's policy framework addresses: (1) AI-assisted dishonesty — by design refusal to generate submittable academic work; (2) Plagiarism prevention — flags pasted external text (15+ words) for teacher review in Writing Coach; (3) Transparency — full conversation logs accessible to teachers, parents, and administrators, eliminating the hidden AI use that characterizes most AI-assisted academic dishonesty.
lich_su_khai_niem: Khanmigo was announced at TED in March 2023 by Sal Khan. It launched in beta March 2023, initially at $4/month for individual users, later made free for students in the US (2024). The product was built in partnership with OpenAI following OpenAI's nonprofit donation to Khan Academy. The Socratic design philosophy predates AI — Khan Academy's pedagogical approach has always emphasized guided discovery over direct instruction. Khanmigo applies this to generative AI, framing it as proof that AI can be deployed responsibly in education.
ten_truong_hop: Khan Academy — Khanmigo, launched March 2023. Global deployment to K-12 students and teachers across Khan Academy's platform. Available as both student-facing tutor and teacher-facing assistant. Free to US students; international availability expanded through Microsoft partnership (2024).
dien_bien: Khan Academy partnered with OpenAI to build Khanmigo, with explicit design constraints to prevent academic dishonesty. Core mechanism: Khanmigo uses a Socratic persona — instead of answering questions directly, it responds with guiding questions that prompt the student to think through problems themselves. For writing tasks, Khanmigo's Writing Coach helps students understand prompts, create outlines, and get feedback on drafts — but will not write the essay itself. If a student pastes 15 or more words from an external source, the passage is flagged for teacher review. All AI-student conversations are logged and visible to educators and parents. This transparency feature fundamentally changes the accountability structure: students cannot use Khanmigo covertly, unlike ChatGPT or other general-purpose AI tools.
ket_qua_xu_ly: No formal disciplinary case — Khanmigo's design prevents misconduct rather than detecting it afterward. Teacher access to full conversation logs means any attempt to misuse Khanmigo (e.g., asking it to write an essay) is visible to educators. The system will notify teachers if safety issues arise with minor users. Khan Academy reports positive reception from educators, with Khanmigo earning 'rave reviews from teachers' since its March 2023 launch. The product is cited frequently in EdTech literature as a model of responsible AI design for education.
con_so_thong_ke: Khan Academy serves over 150 million registered users globally (2024). Khanmigo is available to all US students for free as of 2024. Exact number of active Khanmigo users not publicly disclosed. [uncertain] Khan Academy received $5 million in OpenAI credits and grants to develop Khanmigo. Microsoft partnership (2024) extended Khanmigo access to additional markets globally.
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: Khanmigo's Socratic design is explicitly intended to benefit learners by developing genuine understanding rather than enabling shortcut-taking. The harm risk is minimal by design: students who want to cheat via Khanmigo will be unable to, and those who engage honestly receive pedagogically effective guidance. Potential limitation: students accustomed to immediate AI-generated answers may find Khanmigo's question-based responses frustrating, potentially leading them to use other AI tools instead.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: Khanmigo represents a commercially deployed instance of an integrity-by-design AI system in education. Its success or failure has significant implications for the broader question of whether EdTech AI can be simultaneously useful and resistant to academic dishonesty. No peer-reviewed research specifically on Khanmigo's impact on academic integrity outcomes has been published as of 2025. [uncertain]
hai_cho_xa_hoi: Positive societal impact: Khanmigo demonstrates that AI tools can be deployed in education without enabling mass academic dishonesty, countering the narrative that AI inevitably undermines educational standards. It also addresses equity concerns by providing free AI tutoring to US students who cannot afford private tutors. Risk: if Khanmigo's Socratic approach is perceived as less useful than ChatGPT, students may migrate to less controlled platforms.
cong_cu_phat_hien: Khanmigo is a prevention tool, not a detection tool. Its built-in detection mechanisms are: (1) text-paste flagging — 15+ words pasted from external sources are flagged for teacher review in Writing Coach; (2) conversation logging — all AI-student interactions are recorded and visible to teachers, parents, and administrators; (3) safety alerts — the system notifies teachers of potential safety issues with minor users. Unlike Turnitin or GPTZero, Khanmigo's detection is embedded in the workflow rather than applied after submission.
han_che_cong_cu: Khanmigo's Socratic refusal design has a key limitation: students can use Khanmigo legitimately for tutoring while simultaneously using ChatGPT or another tool to write their actual submission. Khanmigo only controls what happens within its own platform — it cannot detect or prevent use of external AI tools. This means Khanmigo's integrity guarantee applies only to work produced through the Khanmigo interface, not to student work generally. The system is also only as effective as educator engagement with the conversation logs.
watermarking: Khanmigo does not implement LLM watermarking. Its integrity mechanism is conversation transparency and Socratic refusal rather than artifact-based detection. Watermarking (Kirchenbauer/UMD, Aaronson/OpenAI) is designed for detecting AI-generated text in arbitrary submissions — a different point in the integrity workflow. The two approaches are complementary: Khanmigo prevents misconduct within its platform; watermarking could detect AI-generated text submitted from other tools.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: Khanmigo Writing Coach supports process-based writing pedagogy: students work through prompts, outlines, and draft feedback stages with AI guidance, generating a traceable writing process. Teachers receive logs of the entire process, not just the final product. This aligns with the broader recommendation in academic integrity literature (Eaton, 2024; Perkins et al., 2023) to assess process rather than only product. Khanmigo's design is effectively a process-based submission tool with built-in Socratic scaffolding.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: Khanmigo is used in K-12 school settings across the US and internationally. Schools that adopt Khanmigo receive a teacher dashboard with student activity monitoring. Khan Academy's terms of service and educator guidelines specify appropriate use. No single institutional policy document comparable to a university academic integrity policy governs Khanmigo — it operates within existing school AI policies. The product is frequently cited by educators as an example of 'approved AI use' that can be incorporated into school AI policies.
van_hoa_to_chuc: Khanmigo operationalizes McCabe's honor code culture principles at the product design level: rather than relying on student self-regulation or enforcement mechanisms, the system embeds integrity into the interaction design itself. The transparency of conversation logs creates mutual accountability without adversarial surveillance — both students and teachers can see what was discussed, normalizing open AI-assisted learning rather than hiding it.
ai_literacy: Khanmigo is an AI literacy tool by design: students learn how to engage with AI through Socratic dialogue, developing critical thinking about their own reasoning rather than receiving pre-packaged answers. This models appropriate AI use — AI as a thinking partner rather than an answer machine. UNESCO Art. 4 and EU AI Act emphasis on AI literacy align with Khanmigo's pedagogical approach. Sal Khan has explicitly stated the goal is to model how AI should be used in education, not just to deliver content.
khung_quoc_te: Khanmigo aligns with UNESCO 2023 guidance on responsible AI in education: transparency, student agency, pedagogical soundness. The Microsoft partnership (2024) extends the platform's reach globally, including to markets covered by EU AI Act jurisdiction. As a high-stakes decision tool (AI that affects student learning outcomes), Khanmigo potentially falls under EU AI Act Annex III classification — Khan Academy has not publicly addressed EU AI Act compliance. [uncertain]
phap_luat_viet_nam: Khanmigo is available in Vietnam via Khan Academy's international platform and the Microsoft partnership. Vietnamese regulatory framework (Nghị định 109/2022, Điều 20) does not specifically address AI tutoring tools. No Ministry of Education (MOET) guidance specifically endorses or restricts Khanmigo use in Vietnamese schools. The platform's Socratic, non-essay-writing design would likely be viewed favorably under Vietnam's academic integrity norms.
chinh_sach_chau_a: Khan Academy has significant presence in Asia through international partnerships. NUS (Singapore) and other Asian universities reference Khanmigo as a model of responsible AI design in their own AI policy discussions. Specific data on Khanmigo adoption rates at Asian institutions is not publicly available. [uncertain] The Microsoft partnership (2024) facilitates access in Asian markets including Vietnam, India, and South Korea.
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: Khanmigo is the paradigmatic example of Rose Luckin's (UCL) positive framing — AI as democratizing tutor — operationalized in a product that is structurally resistant to the cheating use case Selwyn (Monash) warns about. Sal Khan explicitly argues that AI of the Khanmigo type will 'democratize' access to personalized tutoring that only wealthy families previously could afford. The product demonstrates that the AI tutor / AI cheater binary is not inevitable — design choices determine which the tool becomes.
edtech_company_policies: Khanmigo's policy framework: (1) Socratic design — AI cannot complete assignments for students; (2) Essay refusal — Khanmigo will not write essays or produce submittable academic work; (3) Text-paste flagging — 15+ words from external sources flagged for teacher review; (4) Full conversation transparency — all AI-student dialogue visible to educators, parents, administrators; (5) Safety alerts for minor users. Partnership with OpenAI (technical infrastructure) and Microsoft (distribution). Free for US students since 2024. Available to teachers as classroom assistant with different feature set.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: From an EdTech researcher perspective: (1) Khanmigo demonstrates that integrity-by-design is technically feasible for AI tutoring products — this should become a design standard, not a competitive differentiator; (2) EdTech platforms that allow AI to produce submittable work should face institutional scrutiny; (3) Schools should prefer AI tools with conversation transparency and Socratic constraints over unconstrained general-purpose AI; (4) Research needed: longitudinal studies on whether Khanmigo users show different learning outcomes and academic integrity behavior compared to users of unconstrained AI tools; (5) The AIAS framework (Perkins) should include an assessment of whether EdTech AI tools implement integrity-by-design principles.
